items.stem: Gauri plans a food-processing unit. Costs: land ₹24,50,000, building ₹23,00,000, machinery ₹19,00,000, furniture ₹2,00,000, preliminary expenses ₹1,85,000. Monthly raw material ₹3,65,000, wages ₹60,000 and other expenses ₹35,000; working capital is needed for 2 months. Calculate (a) fixed capital, (b) working capital and (c) total cost of the project.
items.answer: (a) Fixed capital = ₹70,35,000. (b) Working capital = ₹4,60,000 × 2 = ₹9,20,000. (c) Total project cost = ₹79,55,000.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for (a), (b) and (c). (a) Fixed capital = ₹70,35,000. (b) Working capital = ₹4,60,000 × 2 = ₹9,20,000. (c) Total project cost = ₹79,55,000.

items.answer: (a) Fixed capital = ₹91,10,000; working capital = ₹6,20,000 × 1 = ₹6,20,000; total project cost = ₹97,30,000. (b) Means of finance: promoter's capital 25% = ₹24,32,500; bank loan = ₹72,97,500; total = ₹97,30,000.
items.markingKey: (a) 3 marks (1 each), (b) 2 marks. (a) Fixed capital = ₹91,10,000; working capital = ₹6,20,000 × 1 = ₹6,20,000; total project cost = ₹97,30,000. (b) Means of finance: promoter's capital 25% = ₹24,32,500; bank loan = ₹72,97,500; total = ₹97,30,000.

items.stem: Explain any five stages of start-up funding.
items.answer: (i) Bootstrapping: The founder's own money, family and friends. (ii) Seed stage: Funds to develop the idea and build a prototype, often from angel investors. (iii) Early stage (Series A): Funds to start operations and reach customers, often from venture capitalists. (iv) Growth or expansion stage (Series B, C): Funds to scale up, enter new markets and add products. (v) Exit stage: Investors sell their stake through an IPO or acquisition.
items.markingKey: Any five points, 1 mark each (point with a line of explanation): (i) Bootstrapping: The founder's own money, family and friends. (ii) Seed stage: Funds to develop the idea and build a prototype, often from angel investors. (iii) Early stage (Series A): Funds to start operations and reach customers, often from venture capitalists. (iv) Growth or expansion stage (Series B, C): Funds to scale up, enter new markets and add products. (v) Exit stage: Investors sell their stake through an IPO or acquisition.

She will contribute 40% of the project cost as promoter's capital. A government subsidy of 10% of the project cost is available. The rest will be a bank loan. items.answer: (a) Fixed capital = ₹99,85,000; working capital = ₹7,05,000 × 2 = ₹14,10,000; total project cost = ₹1,13,95,000. (b) Means of finance: promoter's capital 40% = ₹45,58,000; subsidy 10% = ₹11,39,500; bank loan = ₹56,97,500; total = ₹1,13,95,000.
items.markingKey: (a) 3 marks (1 each), (b) 2 marks. (a) Fixed capital = ₹99,85,000; working capital = ₹7,05,000 × 2 = ₹14,10,000; total project cost = ₹1,13,95,000. (b) Means of finance: promoter's capital 40% = ₹45,58,000; subsidy 10% = ₹11,39,500; bank loan = ₹56,97,500; total = ₹1,13,95,000.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Shreya started her app with ₹2 lakh of her own savings and reinvested every rupee earned. (a) Which source or stage of funding is shown? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Bootstrapping (b) No outside investors.
items.markingKey: (a) Bootstrapping, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: No outside investors.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the advantages of raising funds through an IPO?
items.answer: Large amount of capital
items.markingKey: (a) "Large amount of capital" is one of the advantages of raising funds through an IPO; the others are limitations of raising funds through an IPO.

items.stem: State one difference between angel investor and venture capitalist on the basis of amount.
items.answer: angel investor: smaller amounts; venture capitalist: larger amounts
items.markingKey: 1 mark: angel investor: smaller amounts; venture capitalist: larger amounts

items.stem: A retired CEO meets Nikhil every month to advise him on strategy. Which non-financial resource is being mobilised? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Mentors. An experienced person gives guidance.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Mentors; 2 marks for the justification: An experienced person gives guidance.

items.stem: Explain "Active participation" with reference to the features of venture capital.
items.answer: Active participation: The investor guides management and may sit on the board.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: The investor guides management and may sit on the board.

items.stem:
Joshi Traders, a growing food-processing company in Shimla, needs ₹40 crore for expansion. Its promoters are thinking of an IPO but worry about the cost, the need to disclose results and the loss of control.
(i) State three advantages of an IPO for Joshi Traders. (ii) State two limitations shown in the case. (iii) Name the regulator.
items.answer: (i) Large capital; no repayment; liquidity; better image; easier future fund-raising (any three). (ii) High cost of issue; strict disclosure; dilution of control (any two). (iii) SEBI.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Large capital; no repayment; liquidity; better image; easier future fund-raising (any three). (ii) High cost of issue; strict disclosure; dilution of control (any two). (iii) SEBI.

items.stem: Ishaan plans a food-processing unit. Costs: land ₹2,00,000, building ₹29,00,000, machinery ₹4,00,000, furniture ₹2,60,000, preliminary expenses ₹1,20,000. Monthly raw material ₹1,30,000, wages ₹75,000 and other expenses ₹20,000; working capital is needed for 2 months. Calculate (a) fixed capital, (b) working capital and (c) total cost of the project.
items.answer: (a) Fixed capital = ₹38,80,000. (b) Working capital = ₹2,25,000 × 2 = ₹4,50,000. (c) Total project cost = ₹43,30,000.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for (a), (b) and (c). (a) Fixed capital = ₹38,80,000. (b) Working capital = ₹2,25,000 × 2 = ₹4,50,000. (c) Total project cost = ₹43,30,000.

items.stem: What is meant by "Crowdfunding"?
items.answer: Raising small amounts of money from a large number of people, usually through an online platform.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Raising small amounts of money from a large number of people, usually through an online platform.

items.stem: Distinguish between incubator and accelerator on the basis of focus, stage and duration.
items.answer: (i) Focus: incubator: building the business; accelerator: rapid growth. (ii) Stage: incubator: very early, idea or prototype stage; accelerator: start-ups with a product and early customers. (iii) Duration: incubator: longer and flexible; accelerator: short, fixed term.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Focus: incubator: building the business; accelerator: rapid growth. (ii) Stage: incubator: very early, idea or prototype stage; accelerator: start-ups with a product and early customers. (iii) Duration: incubator: longer and flexible; accelerator: short, fixed term.

items.stem: Mehta and Sons invited bids between ₹240 and ₹250 per share and fixed the final price from the bids. Which concept is being described?
items.answer: Book building
items.markingKey: (c) Book building. Price is discovered from bids in a band.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about start-up funding is correct?
items.answer: Bootstrapping uses the founder's own resources.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: Bootstrapping uses the founder's own resources.
options: Venture capital is a short-term loan.
Bootstrapping uses the founder's own resources.
Angel investors are banks that give loans.
Seed funding is raised after the IPO.

items.stem: Cost of machinery for the new unit. Is this part of fixed capital or working capital? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Fixed capital. It is a long-term asset.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Fixed capital; 2 marks for the justification: It is a long-term asset.

items.stem: What is meant by "Non-financial resources"?
items.answer: Resources other than money that a start-up needs, such as technology, mentors, networks, people and infrastructure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Resources other than money that a start-up needs, such as technology, mentors, networks, people and infrastructure.

items.stem:
Nair Enterprises, a growing food-processing company in Pune, needs ₹40 crore for expansion. Its promoters are thinking of an IPO but worry about the cost, the need to disclose results and the loss of control.
(i) State three advantages of an IPO for Nair Enterprises. (ii) State two limitations shown in the case. (iii) Name the regulator.
items.answer: (i) Large capital; no repayment; liquidity; better image; easier future fund-raising (any three). (ii) High cost of issue; strict disclosure; dilution of control (any two). (iii) SEBI.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Large capital; no repayment; liquidity; better image; easier future fund-raising (any three). (ii) High cost of issue; strict disclosure; dilution of control (any two). (iii) SEBI.

items.stem: Differentiate between angel investor and venture capitalist with reference to amount and source of money.
items.answer: (i) Amount: angel investor: smaller amounts; venture capitalist: larger amounts. (ii) Source of money: angel investor: personal money; venture capitalist: money pooled from many investors.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Amount: angel investor: smaller amounts; venture capitalist: larger amounts. (ii) Source of money: angel investor: personal money; venture capitalist: money pooled from many investors.

items.stem: Wages to be paid until sales begin to bring in cash. Is this part of fixed capital or working capital?
items.answer: Working capital
items.markingKey: (b) Working capital. It is a day-to-day need.
options: Neither (it is a source of finance)
